ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The fare on this trip was an UPFRONT_QUOTE of SGD 34.50, and under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking. That disposes of the biggest part of the rider's claim: the extra distance you were driven (28.18 km of trace against a 22.4 km optimal route, an excess of 5.78 km / 25.8%) cost you nothing on the distance and time lines — the detour cost fell on the driver — so no distance refund is available however large the excess, and POL-RD-02 does not run. The rider is right that the deviation is nonetheless ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence under POL-RD-01 (both the 0.8 km absolute gate and the 20% proportional gate are cleared, measured on gps_trace.trace_distance_km which governs over the rounded trip-record copy), and the driver is right that it is not MATERIAL (25.8% is below 50% and 5.78 km is below 8.0 km), so no driver-profile check under POL-RD-06 is triggered and no driver-conduct referral arises. The five kilometres of extra driving were not excused: the pool contains no traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and the driver does not ask the tribunal to lean on it; the chat log EV-CHAT-00115 is only the driver's own announcement and the rider's 'ok', with waypoint_hint null on both messages, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to either side. The unchallenged trace — 229 fixes, 100% coverage, 10 s interval, no gaps — is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and needs no independent corroboration. The rider's own profile (deviation_claims_60d 0, substantiated 0) does not raise the POL-RD-08 corroboration bar.

The money that does move is on the pass-through lines, and here both advocates are correct. Of the SGD 4.50 of ERP charged, the SGD 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) gantry is properly chargeable: it lies on the optimal route and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it, inside the 250 m crossing test, so that line stands. The SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry is a phantom line — the nearest fix in the whole trace is 5,419 m away, and the fare ledger itself flags it on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as the billing-integrity referral above. Under POL-RD-11(a) the refund is charged_total less the quote less the properly chargeable pass-through: SGD 39.00 less SGD 34.50 less SGD 2.50 = SGD 2.00. That is the whole of the refund; the distance element of the SGD 6.00 contested is not payable on an upfront-quoted fare, and the driver's denial of the AYE route matches the trace, so no adverse conduct finding attaches to him. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the identifiers and timestamps agree, the trace is unimpaired, the only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and the refund is well within limits.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry line on EV-FARE-00115 is a phantom charge — the GPS trace EV-GPS-00115 never comes within 250 m of that gantry (nearest fix 5,419 m, at the first fix of the trip) — and has been refunded as a standalone correction; the ledger's gantry tagging for this trip requires review.
